meta.label: Car seats
tradeoffLabels: easiest to install and use correctly
meta.attribution: Covers car seats and boosters currently sold in the United States by Britax, Evenflo, Nuna, Clek, Maxi-Cosi, Cosco, Chicco and UPPAbaby: infant seats, convertibles, harness-to-booster seats and belt-positioning boosters. Every seat sold in the US must meet Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 213, the federal crash-performance standard, so nothing here ranks one seat as safer in a crash than another. NHTSA's own advice is that a seat works best when it is correctly installed and the child is correctly secured, and that its ratings measure ease of use, not safety. This is not safety advice for a specific child: follow the seat's manual, its height and weight limits and your vehicle's manual, and a certified child passenger safety technician can check an installation. METHOD. Recall record (the safety key) comes from NHTSA's recall database: 90 when NHTSA's recall flat file, current to 8 October 2026, lists no child restraint recall naming the model since January 2016; 70 for one campaign; 50 for two or more. Each note says what the recall was, because a missing registration card and a harness defect are very different things. The IIHS booster belt-fit ratings are not used: IIHS says it ran them from 2008 to 2024 and no longer does. Ease of use (accessibility) is NHTSA's Car Seat Ease-of-Use rating, read from NHTSA's car seat API (api.nhtsa.gov/childSeats, whose record numbers change between releases, so entries are matched by make, model name and model number): the average of the overall star ratings across the modes NHTSA rated, times 20, so five stars is 100. A rating is used only where NHTSA's record names the same model, and the note gives the model number and the date of the seat NHTSA rated. Price (economical) is the list price on the maker's own US store in October 2026, scored as 100 minus 0.15 per dollar, so $20 scores 97 and $500 scores 25; boosters are naturally cheaper than infant or convertible seats, so compare within a seat type. Useful life (longevity) is the expiry the maker publishes, on its product page or in the US manual, at 10 points per year, so a 10-year seat scores 100; no score is given where the maker only points to the date label. Not scored: crash-test results beyond FMVSS 213, fit in any particular car, and fabrics or chemical treatments, which are mentioned in descriptions only. Graco, the largest US brand, is left out for now because its website could not be read from here to confirm current models, prices or expiry; Cybex, Diono, Doona and Safety 1st are left out because their current US models are not the ones NHTSA rated, or no US price could be read from the maker. Sources: NHTSA (Ease-of-Use ratings, recall campaigns and the recall flat file), IIHS, and each maker's US product pages and manuals. Not safety advice. Reviewed 2026-10. Suggest changes via Contribute.

criteria.label: Ease of installing and using correctly (NHTSA)

products.name: Britax Poplar
products.description: A slim 17-inch convertible seat with ClickTight belt installation, rear-facing to 50 lb and forward-facing to 65 lb.

safety.note: NHTSA's recall file, current to 8 October 2026, lists no child seat recall naming the Poplar since 2016. Britax's recall that August covered B-Safe Gen 2 infant seats, not this model.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Britax Poplar (model E1C933QDI, rated on a seat made 2024-06) gives rear-facing 4 stars, forward-facing 3 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. NHTSA notes the lower attachments require twisting to remove and the forward-facing belt lockoff may be confusing.

economical.note: Britax's US store lists the Poplar at $349.99.

longevity.note: Britax's product page gives 'Expiration: 10 Years' for the Poplar.

products.name: Britax Willow S
products.description: A rear-facing infant seat sold with the Alpine base, which has a stability bar, for babies from 4 to 30 lb.

safety.note: NHTSA's recall file, current to 8 October 2026, has no child seat recall naming the Willow S since 2016.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Britax Willow S (model E1C993XDI, rated on a seat made 2024-07) gives rear-facing 4 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. Vehicle installation features earn five stars; securing the child earns three, partly because the harness must be rethreaded as the baby grows.

economical.note: Britax's US store lists the Willow S with Alpine base at $279.99.

longevity.note: Britax's product page gives 'Expiration: 6 Years' for the Willow S.

products.name: Britax Cypress
products.description: A rear-facing infant seat with a lightweight aluminium handle, sold with the Alpine base.

safety.note: NHTSA's recall file, current to 8 October 2026, shows no child seat recall naming the Cypress since 2016.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Britax Cypress, Alpine Base (model E1D124Y, rated on a seat made 2024-03) gives rear-facing 5 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. NHTSA rated the Cypress with its Alpine base; instructions, labels and installation each earn five stars.

economical.note: Britax's US store lists the Cypress at $379.99.

longevity.note: Britax's product page lists 'Expiration: 6 Years' for the Cypress.

products.name: Britax Grow With You ClickTight
products.description: A harness-to-booster seat: forward-facing with a five-point harness first, then a high-back booster up to 120 lb.

safety.note: NHTSA's recall file, current to 8 October 2026, holds no child seat recall naming the Grow With You since 2016.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Britax Grou With You Clicktight (model E1C199L, rated on a seat made 2019-08) gives forward-facing 5 stars, booster 4 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. NHTSA's record spells the name 'Grou With You Clicktight'. Booster-mode securing scores one star because conversion steps are not illustrated on the seat.

economical.note: Britax's US store lists the Grow With You ClickTight at $349.99.

longevity.note: Britax's product page gives 'Expiration: 9 Years' for this model.

products.name: Britax Highpoint
products.description: A two-stage belt-positioning booster, high-back from 40 lb and backless from 48 lb, up to 120 lb.

safety.note: NHTSA's recall file, current to 8 October 2026, shows no child seat recall naming the Highpoint since 2016.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Britax Highpoint (model E1C238T, rated on a seat made 2020-06) gives booster 4 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. A second NHTSA Highpoint record (model E1C233D, rated 2022) also gives four stars.

economical.note: Britax's US store lists the Highpoint at $219.99.

longevity.note: Britax's product page gives 'Expiration: 10 Years' for the Highpoint.

products.name: Britax Skyline
products.description: A lower-priced two-stage Britax booster that converts from high-back to backless.

safety.note: NHTSA's recall file, current to 8 October 2026, lists no child seat recall naming the Skyline since 2016.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Britax Skyline (model E1C269H, rated on a seat made 2021-01) gives booster 4 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. Installation features earn five stars; NHTSA notes the back was not attached when removed from the packaging.

economical.note: Britax's US store lists the Skyline at $139.99.

products.name: Evenflo NurtureMax
products.description: A budget rear-facing infant seat for babies from 4 to 22 lb, light at about 9 lb with its base.

safety.note: NHTSA's recall file, current to 8 October 2026, holds no child seat recall naming the NurtureMax; it was not among the models in Evenflo's 2025 registration-card recall.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Evenflo NurtureMax (model 36412348, rated on a seat made 2022-06) gives rear-facing 3 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. Securing the child earns two stars: the harness must be rethreaded as the baby grows and the buckle tongues must be held together to insert.

economical.note: Evenflo's US store lists the NurtureMax at $74.99, among the cheapest infant seats here.

longevity.note: For the NurtureMax, Evenflo's guidance, dated March 2026, applies: it says 'all of our car seats and booster seats now have a 10 year expiration from the date of manufacture', and that seats made before January 2025 may differ, so the label on an older seat governs.

products.name: Evenflo Tribute LX
products.description: A low-cost, lightweight convertible seat, rear-facing from 5 lb and forward-facing to 40 lb.

safety.note: NHTSA campaign 25C003, March 2025, covered Evenflo seats including the Tribute that shipped without the US recall registration card, a compliance failure under FMVSS 213; Evenflo mailed cards free. No crash-performance defect was alleged.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Evenflo Tribute (model 38111190, rated on a seat made 2025-05) gives rear-facing 2 stars, forward-facing 2 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. Labels and installation features each earn one star; NHTSA notes 'It may be uncomfortable for those with larger hands to route the seat belt or LATCH belt through the belt path.' Evenflo's Tribute LX listing (CS200211190) shares the 11190 code of the rated model 38111190.

economical.note: Evenflo's US store lists the Tribute LX at $99.99.

longevity.note: For the Tribute LX, Evenflo's guidance, dated March 2026, applies: it says 'all of our car seats and booster seats now have a 10 year expiration from the date of manufacture', and that seats made before January 2025 may differ, so the label on an older seat governs.

products.name: Evenflo Chase Plus
products.description: A low-cost harness-to-booster seat: forward-facing harness from 22 lb, then a belt-positioning booster to 120 lb.

safety.note: NHTSA's recall file, current to 8 October 2026, holds no child seat recall naming the Chase Plus since 2016; an earlier Evenflo campaign in 2014 named the older Chase.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Evenflo Chase Plus (model 30712360, rated on a seat made 2021-02) gives forward-facing 2 stars, booster 3 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. Forward-facing labels earn one star; NHTSA notes the hook-style LATCH attachments may require twisting to remove.

economical.note: Evenflo's US store lists the Chase Plus at $64.99.

longevity.note: For the Chase Plus, Evenflo's guidance, dated March 2026, applies: it says 'all of our car seats and booster seats now have a 10 year expiration from the date of manufacture', and that seats made before January 2025 may differ, so the label on an older seat governs.

products.name: Evenflo Maestro Sport
products.description: A harness-to-booster seat from 22 lb in harness mode to 110 lb as a high-back booster.

safety.note: NHTSA campaign 25C003, March 2025, named the Maestro among Evenflo seats shipped without the US recall registration card; Evenflo mailed replacement cards free of charge. The defect was the missing card, not the seat.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Evenflo Maestro Sport (model 34912366, rated on a seat made 2022-06) gives forward-facing 2 stars, booster 4 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. Booster mode earns four stars, harness mode two, because the harness must be rethreaded and slots are hidden by the head support.

economical.note: Evenflo's US store lists the Maestro Sport at $119.99.

longevity.note: For the Maestro Sport, Evenflo's guidance, dated March 2026, applies: it says 'all of our car seats and booster seats now have a 10 year expiration from the date of manufacture', and that seats made before January 2025 may differ, so the label on an older seat governs.

products.name: Nuna PIPA rx
products.description: A premium rear-facing infant seat sold with the RELX base, which reclines and has a load leg; it can also be installed without a base.

safety.note: NHTSA's recall file, current to 8 October 2026, has no child seat recall naming the PIPA rx or any PIPA model since 2016.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Nuna Pipa rx (model CF12508607BLK, rated on a seat made 2023-11) gives rear-facing 4 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. NHTSA notes the lower anchor storage is not clearly labeled and the harness must be rethreaded to change height.

economical.note: Nuna's US site lists the PIPA rx with RELX base from $409.99.

products.name: Nuna RAVA
products.description: A premium convertible seat, rear-facing to 50 lb and forward-facing to 65 lb, slim enough for three across in many full-size cars.

safety.note: NHTSA campaign 24C002, November 2024, recalled about 609,000 RAVA seats made between July 2016 and October 2023, because debris may enter the plastic harness adjuster and leave the harness loose; Nuna supplies a free remedy kit.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Nuna rava (model CS05103CVR, rated on a seat made 2021-08) gives rear-facing 3 stars, forward-facing 3 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. Rear-facing installation features earn one star; NHTSA notes the padding may need moving and there is nothing on the seat that gives immediate feedback on a correct install.

economical.note: Nuna's US site lists the RAVA from $480, the dearest convertible here.

longevity.note: Nuna's US RAVA manual for 2024 and newer seats says 'Do not use child restraint if it is more than 10 years old.'

products.name: Nuna AACE
products.description: A high-back booster that converts to backless, with rigid lower-anchor connectors and an eight-position recline.

safety.note: NHTSA's recall file, current to 8 October 2026, lists no child seat recall naming the AACE since 2016.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Nuna aace (model CS07007GRN, rated on a seat made 2021-12) gives booster 4 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. Installation features earn five stars; securing the child earns two, as NHTSA found no labels showing how to convert to backless mode.

economical.note: Nuna's US site lists the AACE from $300.

longevity.note: Nuna's US AACE manual says 'DO NOT use booster if it is more than 10 years old.'

products.name: Clek Fllo
products.description: A narrow Canadian-made convertible seat, rear-facing from 14 lb and forward-facing to 65 lb, often chosen for three-across fits.

safety.note: NHTSA campaign 21C005, December 2021, recalled Foonf and Fllo seats made before 21 May 2021 (Fllo models FL15 to FL19) because a child could pick pieces of foam from the cushion under the seat pad; Clek supplied a plastic insert free.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Clek Fllo (model fl19u1, rated on a seat made 2024-08) gives rear-facing 3 stars, forward-facing 3 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. Forward-facing labels earn one star; NHTSA notes the padding must be removed to route the belt and the lock-off is confusing.

economical.note: Clek's US store lists the Fllo at $499.99, the dearest seat here.

longevity.note: Clek's product page states 'Fllo has a 9 year expiration.'

products.name: Clek Liingo
products.description: A rear-facing infant seat that installs with the vehicle belt and a built-in lock-off, with no base.

safety.note: Two NHTSA campaigns in December 2021 covered the Liingo (model LGO20U1): 21C006, for a canopy-support piece that could break off on seats made before 15 September 2020, and 21C007, for labels that could bubble up and come apart on seats made before 22 February 2021. Both remedies were free.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Clek Liingo (model LGO20U1, rated on a seat made 2021-06) gives rear-facing 3 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. Instructions earn five stars; labels earn two.

economical.note: Clek's US store lists the Liingo at $399.99.

longevity.note: Clek's product page states 'Liingo has a 9 year expiration.'

products.name: Clek Oobr
products.description: A full-size high-back booster with rigid lower-anchor connectors and a reclining back that converts to backless.

safety.note: NHTSA's recall file, current to 8 October 2026, shows no child seat recall naming the Oobr; Clek's 2022 label recall named the Olli and Ozzi only.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Clek Oobr (model S22146826, rated on a seat made 2022-06) gives booster 3 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. Instructions earn five stars; securing the child earns one, as NHTSA found no illustration of the high-back to backless conversion on the label.

economical.note: Clek's US store lists the Oobr from $399.99, the dearest booster here.

longevity.note: Clek's product page states 'Oobr has a 9 year expiration.'

products.name: Clek Ozzi
products.description: A backless booster with rigid lower-anchor connectors, for children from 40 to 120 lb.

safety.note: NHTSA campaign 22C002, June 2022, recalled Ozzi boosters (model OZ11U2) made between March 2020 and May 2022 because the diagram showing installation with a continuous-loop lap and shoulder belt was missing, a labelling noncompliance under FMVSS 213; Clek mailed new labels.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Clek Ozzi (model OZ11U2, rated on a seat made 2025-03) gives booster 5 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. Securing the child and instructions each earn five stars; installation is rated not applicable.

economical.note: Clek's US store lists the Ozzi at $129.99.

longevity.note: Clek's product page states 'Ozzi has a 9 year expiration.'

products.name: Maxi-Cosi RodiSport
products.description: A 2-in-1 belt-positioning booster, high-back then backless, from Dorel Juvenile, which also owns Safety 1st and Cosco.

safety.note: NHTSA's recall file, current to 8 October 2026, has no child seat recall naming the RodiSport since 2016; the 2023 Maxi-Cosi recall covered infant seat bases.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Maxi-Cosi RodiSport (model BC152FNC, rated on a seat made 2021-10) gives booster 4 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. Securing the child and instructions each earn five stars; NHTSA notes 'The shoulder belt guide may allow unintentional slack to occur in the seat belt.'

economical.note: Maxi-Cosi's US store lists the RodiSport (item BC152, the same model family NHTSA rated) at $199.99.

longevity.note: The RodiSport manual linked from Maxi-Cosi's product page says not to use the seat 'more than 10 years after the date of manufacture'.

products.name: Cosco Topside
products.description: The cheapest seat here: a basic backless booster for children from 40 to 100 lb, made in the USA by Dorel Juvenile.

safety.note: NHTSA's recall file, current to 8 October 2026, has no child seat recall naming the Topside since 2016.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Cosco Top Side (model BC030CMM, rated on a seat made 2021-12) gives booster 5 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. A backless booster has no vehicle installation features to rate; securing the child and instructions each earn five stars.

economical.note: Cosco's US store lists the Topside BC030, the model number NHTSA rated, at $22.99; a newer BC214 version is listed at $19.99.

longevity.note: Cosco's 2026 Rise LX and Topside booster manual says not to use the booster 'more than 10 years after the date of manufacture'. The manual linked from the BC030 listing points to the date label instead, so this is the current Topside manual rather than the rated BC030 printing.

products.name: Chicco GoFit
products.description: A backless booster with a contoured double-foam seat, for children from 40 to 110 lb.

safety.note: NHTSA's recall file, current to 8 October 2026, lists no child seat recall naming the GoFit; Chicco's only child seat recall in the period was the MyFit in 2025.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the Chicco GoFit (model 4.07975E+12, rated on a seat made 2022-03) gives booster 5 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. Securing the child, instructions and labels earn four or five stars each.

economical.note: Chicco's US store lists the GoFit at $54.99.

products.name: UPPAbaby Alta V2
products.description: A high-back booster with a belt-routing guide, GREENGUARD Gold certified fabrics and no added fire retardants.

safety.note: NHTSA's recall file, current to 8 October 2026, holds no child seat recall naming UPPAbaby since 2016.

accessibility.note: NHTSA's Ease-of-Use rating for the UPPAbaby Alta V2 (model 1320-ALT-US-JKE, rated on a seat made 2025-04) gives booster 3 stars overall, out of five; the score here is the average of those overall stars times 20. Installation features earn five stars; securing the child and labels earn two. NHTSA's model number reads 1320-ALT-US-JKE, UPPAbaby's listing 1302-ALT-US-JKE.

economical.note: UPPAbaby's US site lists the Alta V2 at $199.99.

longevity.note: UPPAbaby's Alta V2 manual sets a limit of '10 years from date of manufacture'.
